text:
mike: heads-up — after the kernel-selection change merged yesterday I'm seeing a p50 jump on the small-chat workload. quick nsys attached: https://internal.artifacts/nsys/1778001111.trace :eyes:

liz: link looks like the one i grabbed. what numbers are you seeing?

mike: baseline p50 was ~68ms, after change it's ~83ms. tail worse. throughput unchanged. heap of queue time in the timeline.

rahul: interesting — did the selector flip from fast-f32 matmul to int8 gemm on that model? that can change grooming of the batching window.

mike: yep selector picked quantized-gemm variant when seq_len<=64. suspected it but nvprof/nsys show long host->device enqueue gaps. timeline snippet:

```
# nsys timeline (abridged)
Host enqueue -> 0.0ms
cudaMemcpyAsync (kv_copy) -> 2.3ms
multi_head_attention_int8 -> 5.6ms
Host enqueue (batch flush) -> 48.7ms  <-- big idle
matmul_int8 -> 50.0ms
softmax -> 52.1ms
```

mike: queue gap around 40-45ms per request. that's the regression.

jena: can you share the full perfetto link? want to check CPU-side batching loop. sometimes the quantized path adds extra memcpy or synchronization.

mike: perfetto: https://perfetto.local/trace/1778001111 — i see a blocking syscall from the batching thread right before the gap. looks like an extra memcpy + kernel launch ordering.

liz: that syscall could be from the runtime deciding to wait for kernel completion to recycle scratch buffers. did we change scratch pooling with the new kernel?

rahul: also check KV cache behavior — if kv-lookup returns miss, we do an extra memcpy to allocate. did the selector change cause different cache alignment?

mike: KV hitrate was stable but the int8 path does a different packing step for KV prefetch which triggers an extra host memcpy per request. small sequences amplify this.

jena: ok. proposed steps:
- reproduce with nsys but set env REDWOOD_BATCH_WINDOW=8ms and 40ms to compare
- force selector to old gemm and repro to confirm correlation
- capture perf counters (SM occupancy) to rule out kernel slowness

mike: ran quick A/B: forcing old gemm returns p50 to ~69ms. forcing int8 but with packing disabled reduces gap to ~6ms and p50 to ~71ms.

liz: so culprit = packing + memcpy in int8 path causing host queue stall. two fixes: remove memcpy by doing in-place pack on GPU, or adjust batching heuristics to expand continuous window to absorb packing latency.

rahul: in-place GPU packing seems like more robust fix but takes more dev time. for short term we can tweak selector to avoid int8 below seq_len 48 and bump batch window to 12ms to keep latency tight.

perf-bot: perf regression alert created: INC-2026. Attached artifacts: nsys trace, perfetto trace, p50/p95 before & after.

mike: i'll open PR that toggles selector threshold + add a metric for host-queue-time so we can alert if it creeps up.

jena: i'll prototype GPU packing rn — got a simple kernel sketch that can pack KV into quantized layout without host memcpy. will ping when i have numbers.

liz: awesome. keep comms short in the PR and add the nsys diff. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — will post updates here when PRs and perf runs land.
